newsitem.title: UK: BZW's new head makes top management change.
newsitem.headline: BZW's new head makes top management change.

text.p: Bill Harrison, the new head of BZW, the investment banking arm of British bank Barclays Plc, on Thursday unveiled his new-look management team.

But there was no room in Harrison's front-line for Barclays veteran Donald Brydon, who has been acting chief executive of the firm for the last six months following the sudden death of chief executive David Band in March.

BZW said Brydon, who was Band's deputy and joined the Barclays group in 1977, had agreed to leave the firm. At the time of Harrison's appointment in June it said he would remain as deputy chief executive, but this position has now been cut.
Harrison was brought in from British merchant bank Robert Fleming as Band's replacement as head of the fast expanding BZW. Band died while on a family skiing holiday in France.
At the time of his appointment Harrison told Reuters he was lured from Flemings by the challenge of a fiercely competitive market and the nature, scale and reach of the BZW business.

There was intense speculation at the time of his appointment over Harrison's pay package, although attention has since switched to how much a more recent hire, Bob Diamond, is earning. As a director of Barclays, Harrison's pay will be published with the group's annual report and accounts.
One report suggested Diamond, who became chief executive of the global markets division in July, had signed a five million stg package over two years.
Since his appointment, Diamond has been active in hiring and firing, although BZW insiders say the uncertainty created by his appointment has now diminished.
As part of today's reshuffle, Diamond has been brought onto BZW's management committee, the only outsider apart from Harrison to have joined the body.
BZW also said its head of equities Jonathan Davie had stepped down. It said he had already expressed a desire to do so at the end of the remuneration round in February 1997.

"It has been agreed that this date be brought forward and that Steve Harker, his current deputy, becomes the chief executive of equities and a member of the management committee with immediate effect," the company added.
Davie has been made full-time deputy chairman.

Patrick O'Sullivan, currently chief executive of structured finance, has been appointed chief operating officer and will join the management committee along with David Cannon, finance director, and Sally Bott, head of Human Resources. Harrison said he had "decided to strengthen the senior management team and bring additional skills and experience onto the management committee."

He said Brydon "has served BZW and the group well in building the asset management business and also during the last six months in his role as acting chief executive. We wish him well for the future."

Brydon, who was not immediately available for comment, said in a statement that BZW was in good shape and had "a vigorous new management team to take it forward in the next stage of its development." ($1=.6430 Pound)
